newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL - SISTER OF RAPTORS' CARLOS ROGERS DIES.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL - SISTER OF RAPTORS' CARLOS ROGERS DIES.

text.p: The sister of Toronto Raptors forward Carlos Rogers, who had volunteered to donate a kidney to her even if it meant ending his young NBA career, has died of a blood infection. She was 29.
Rene Rogers died in Henry Ford Hospital Friday afternoon of a septic infection, a spokesman for the Detroit hospital said.
"My sister fought a long and hard battle. It's kind of hard to sit here now and talk about it," Carlos Rogers said at a hospital news conference.

The 25-year-old player, in his third season in the NBA, had left the Raptors Thursday afternoon ready and willing to donate his kidney to his ailing sister. But he was unable to do so as her condition worsened, preventing any transplant.
"I would like to thank everybody for supporting me in my decision," Rogers said.
"I feel that any sane person would do it for their family. I don't think I did anything that any ordinary person wouldn't do."
He has said he was the only one in his family -- he has 10 brothers and sisters -- whose kidney would be compatible with his sister's immune system.
"It's difficult to continue to smile and act as though you're happy when you know your sister is suffering," the normally outgoing player said.
"I'm a true believer that God would never give you anything that you can't handle. So He did what was best for my sister, and the family as well because it's a difficult thing to watch."

The 6-foot-11 (2.11 metres) player, whose salary this season is $1.14 million, has four children and also helps support his mother and many of his siblings. He had said donating a kidney would not necessarily end his career.

Rene Rogers was on dialysis when she contracted the blood infection and slipped into critical condition Thursday. She had suffered kidney problems for more than 10 years and received a transplant four years ago, but that new kidney had started to fail.

Toronto general manager Isiah Thomas had said the Raptors organisation would stand behind Rogers no matter what happened, and that the team would have honoured the remainder of his contract in the event that a kidney donation had taken place and cut the player's career short.

Rogers is averaging 10.5 points and 5.8 rebounds a game this season. Counting this season, he has seven years and more than $12 million coming on a contract he signed in 1994 with the Golden State Warriors.
